thread:
alexa: noticed an anomaly in object metadata during a compliance scan. Found several GCS blobs labeled with a deleted KMS key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/integrations/cryptoKeys/legacy-wrap-2024. Could affect partner delivery restores.

alexa: snippet of `gsutil stat` output:
```
Name: gs://partner-archive/integrations/2024-11-02/package-v2.tar.gz
Storage class: STANDARD
Encryption: Customer-supplied KMS
Metadata: envelope.wrap_key=projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/integrations/cryptoKeys/legacy-wrap-2024
```

alexa: This looks like a wrap-key deletion event from late 2024. @dmitri can you confirm whether the key was intentionally destroyed?

dmitri: I see an audit log entry: `kms.cryptoKeys.destroy` for legacy-wrap-2024 on 2024-12-05T17:22:10Z performed by svcacc-deploy. We did a rekey, but the migration note said we archived objects first. Clearly some objects were missed.

liu: critical question: do we have any plaintext producers (CI jobs or partner systems) that still retain the original package? If so, we should ask for a re-push instead of doing controlled decrypt.

alexa: partner-app team owns the original builds. I've alerted them in #partners.

ops-bot: PagerDuty incident created: SEC-GCS-LEGACYWRAP-2024 (priority: P3)

dmitri: suggested course of action: 1) enumerates objects referencing legacy-wrap-2024, 2) snapshot object hashes and metadata to sec-audit-bucket (readonly), 3) ask partner-app for original artifacts, 4) if partner can't provide, escalate for controlled rewrap via legal approved process.

alexa: add: include a 3rd party vendor notification if partner artifacts were transferred off our infra. compliance, please advise on notification thresholds. @compliance

compliance: vendor notification depends on contract terms. We need to know if these artifacts contain customer PII or credentials. Please tag suspected files with sensitivity labels and collect a quick data classification report.

liu: I've run a grep over object metadata; found 9 objects in partner-archive and 3 in partner-prod. Uploading list to the incident.

dmitri: I'll prepare a terraform snippet to create a temporary decrypt-only KMS key policy for `rewrap-job` that is heavily time-limited and requires an HSM audit log. But note: you cannot decrypt if the original key material is destroyed. This only helps if the key was disabled or scheduled for destroy but not yet destroyed.

alexa: good point. I'll fetch the KMS key state.

alexa: KMS state: legacy-wrap-2024 status=DESTROYED (confirmed). So decrypt path using KMS is impossible. We need either original plaintext or backups.

liu: backup catalog check: found archive-store backups for that date range, but they are snapshotted with the envelope metadata preserved. No plaintext.

dmitri: then the only realistic options are: A) get original producers to re-push artifacts re-encrypted with integrations-wrap-v2; B) mark artifacts as unrecoverable and produce a data loss statement + mitigation plan.

alexa: business owner (partner-integrations) responded: they confirm they have rebuild capability but need 24-48h to validate. They'll repush if all good.

compliance: flag: if artifacts were part of any customer deliverable, we must notify customers per SLA. Need to confirm scope before notifying.

ops-bot: Note: created JIRA SEC-2025-289 for tracking.

liu: I'll prepare a minimal reingest playbook for partner-app: commands to re-encrypt on their side and upload:
```
# example rewrap on partner side
gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=integrations --key=integrations-wrap-v2 --plaintext-file=package-v2.tar.gz --ciphertext-file=package-v2.tar.gz.enc
gsutil cp package-v2.tar.gz.enc gs://partner-prod-bucket/integrations/2024-11-02/
```
Include checksums in upload metadata.

dmitri: also recommend we add a preventative test in the release pipeline to detect envelope references to deprecated keys and fail the job. I'll open a PR to the infra repo.

alexa: OK. Action items:
- dmitri: infra PR to add envelope detection & CI fail (ETA 4h)
- liu: upload object list + sensitivity tag report to SEC-2025-289 (ETA 30m)
- partner-integrations: verify backups/rebuild and re-push artifacts (ETA 48h)
- compliance: confirm customer notification thresholds once we have data classification (ETA when list present)

alexa: closing loop: if producers re-push, we'll verify checksums and rotate any affected object metadata. If not, we'll declare unrecoverable and run retrospective to tighten RBAC and rekeying process.

compliance: acknowledged. keep SEC-2025-289 updated.
